sources.cite: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026. Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1):S132-S149
sources.note: Relayed from the FNP (professional role) case clinic-sulfonylurea-hypoglycemia, not re-read for this band; its note: Read directly 2026-11-16 on PMC (primary text, summarizing fetch with quotes); it matches the LPN/VN case's 2026-11-11 reading. Level 1 glucose <70 and >=54 mg/dL, level 2 <54, level 3 a severe event needing assistance; glucose preferred for the conscious person below 70, 15 g for most, recheck 15 minutes after and repeat if still low; glucagon for those unable to take carbohydrate by mouth. Rec. 6.19: 'One or more episodes of level 2 or 3 hypoglycemia should prompt reevaluation of the treatment plan, including deintensifying or switching diabetes medications if appropriate'; 6.6: 'Deintensify hypoglycemia-causing medications (insulin, sulfonylureas, or meglitinides), or switch to a medication class with lower hypoglycemia risk'; 'Hypoglycemia is the major risk to individuals treated with insulin, sulfonylureas, or meglitinides.' Stopping the glipizide and choosing a lower-risk agent follows 6.6 and 6.19.

Relayed from the FNP (professional role) case clinic-sulfonylurea-hypoglycemia, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the course seed (read 2026-11-07). Level 1 below 70 mg/dL, level 2 below 54; 15 g fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck in 15 minutes; glucagon if the person cannot take carbohydrate by mouth.
